descriptionHtml:
Bug B33 · P2 · new

A wrong device clock breaks sign-in and dictation: a 12+ hour jump signs the physician out on reload (the server session is still valid); a clock 70+ s fast makes every dictation fail with 'couldn't start'

Tickets: TFA-94513 in progress; TFA-94423 ready for qa · counts as a QA bug: partly · found on: local

Other cases of the same bug (counted once): TC-23/S24

Approach · OAT-01 Signing In & Session Security · S07 Edges no test asserts yet: a session just under 30 days, the code's 5 minutes and 3 attempts, a failed code email, and a wrong browser clock

UAT steps / ticket ACs covered:

  • U1 Sign-in is by email one-time passcode only: no password field and no shared or static PIN anywhere. The only exception is the two app review accounts, which use a fixed code. (UAT OAT-01 step 1; UAT OAT-01 Expected; TFA-94513 AC 1) — gate: blocked: TFA-94513 in progress
  • U3 After 12 hours idle, the physician has to sign in again with an email OTP. (UAT OAT-01 step 3; UAT OAT-01 Expected; TFA-94513 AC 4) — gate: blocked: TFA-94513 in progress
  • U4 At 30 days the session hard-expires, however active it is. On day 31, access needs a new email OTP. (UAT OAT-01 step 4; UAT OAT-01 Expected; TFA-94513 AC 5) — gate: blocked: TFA-94513 in progress

Test design technique: Boundary values (boundary) — Sit right on the edge of the rule (exactly on time / a minute late, empty, longest, most) and see on which side the behavior changes.

Given API clients for fresh @roundai.test accounts on the local stack (admin key for the test-only helpers). Cell (d) on an isolated stack with AUTH_EMAIL_PROVIDER unset, so convex/email.ts throws. Cell (e) in a Playwright context with page.clock.install and timezoneId.

When (a) sessions:_backdateForTests {createdAt: now - 30 d + 1 h, expiresAt: now + 11 h}, then settings:get. (b) Use a code from seed:issueTestOtp at 4 min 59 s; use another after its verification row's expiresAt is past 5 min. (c) Enter three wrong codes, then the correct one; …

Then (a) settings:get resolves: a session 30 d - 1 h old still works. (b) Accepted at 4:59, refused after 5:00. (c) The correct code after three wrong ones is refused; a new code is needed and works. (d) The screen does not claim a code was sent; it says the email could not be sent (wording per Q17). …

Pass rule (oracle, excerpt): U4 (hard expiry at 30 d, not earlier: a 24 h or 7 d ceiling fails (a)). U1 (a code that never expires or allows unlimited guesses works like a static PIN): (b) and (c) test the build's own values, which Q12 may change. U1 and the 'send errors are swallowed' risk for (d), with the wording left to Q17. …

Where it ran: local newspec-a (new Playwright specs); test method API · API (Convex functions); lane planned in the matrix: existing tests (Tim's Playwright) (blocked)

S07 is our own case number (its number in the coverage matrix cases/OAT-01.matrix.json), not a step number of the UAT document.

Triage (2026-10-14): 1 row.

Issue type: New product issue · environment local · tickets TFA-94513 in progress; TFA-94659 ready for qa

A physician who signed in normally lands on the sign-in screen after a reload once the device clock jumps forward about 12 h or more (for example a phone that resyncs its time), even though the server session is still valid.

Evidence: allure 2c8f0558-…-result.json; runs/2026-10-14-local/newspec-a (incl. rerun-under-load.log). Cell (e): +13 h and +31 d lead to sign-in while get-session with the old token still answers; -2 d keeps the list. The web client stores the session cookie in localStorage with expiry = sign-in + 12 h by the device clock. Seen in 3 runs and in the reviewer's probe. This breaks UAT 3.8 and the S07 oracle ('a sign-out caused only by the browser clock = Fail'). Not in the dev report, ledger or matrix. Cells a–c pass. Cell (d) is known (TFA-94659 note, wording pending Q17): when the code email cannot be sent the screen still says 'Check your email for a 6-digit code'. Gate TFA-94513 is in progress, but its remaining work is invites, disabling accounts, the fixed code and dates, not this.

Environment: local — main e02167f → 25acd727 (10-15/16/17 re-tests), local stack (not a deployed build); run folder runs/2026-10-14-local, lane newspec-a.

Test method: API · API (Convex functions); secondary: TIME · Time / aging (clock moved) — as classified in cases/test-methods.json, which says it runs on local; Source: newspec-a.

UAT item: OAT-01 Signing In & Session Security · Section: B · Operational Acceptance Tests · Scenario: OAT-01/S07

Edges no test asserts yet: a session just under 30 days, the code's 5 minutes and 3 attempts, a failed code email, and a wrong browser clock

Tickets: TFA-94513 Signing In & Session Security (in progress)

New local lane newspec-a: status failed in newspec-a/results.json → failed · product (failed · product (the lane flagged a product issue; part of it is a known gap)).

How it is tested (newspec-a/plan.json, automatable: yes): New spec: (a) sessions:_backdateForTests createdAt=now-30d+1h then settings:get resolves (contrast 30 d + 1 min refused); (b) two codes for two fresh accounts, real wait: one used at 4:58 after issue (upper bound of its age), one when its age is >= 5:02; assert 200, then 400 OTP_EXPIRED or INVALID_OTP; (c) three wrong codes (400 INVALID_OTP each), then the correct one (must be 403 TOO_MANY_ATTEMPTS), then a fresh code works (200); (d) on the ISOLATED backend with AUTH_EMAIL_PROVIDER unset (email.ts throws): press Send sign-in code in the browser, read what the screen says; (e) MAIN: sign in through the form at the right clock (Pacific/Honolulu), then move the browser clock +13 h / +31 d / -2 d and reload: the list must stay (server session state read with get-session); plus a session aged on the server (expiresAt = now-1 s) with the clock set back must show sign-in. EXTRA variant only: sign in on a browser whose clock is already wrong (cannot show a clock-caused sign-out). — Test-only session hooks exist on the local stack; the 5-minute code window is a bounded real wait; the failed send needs a backend without an email provider, which I start myself.

Detail:

(a) pass: a session 30 d - 1 h old resolves settings:get; 30 d + 1 min is refused 'session too_old'. (b) pass: a code sent 298.0 s after issue (answered at 300.2 s, upper bound of its age) accepted 200; another whose age was >= 302 s refused 400 INVALID_OTP (OTP_EXPIRED is also accepted by the test: Better Auth removes the expired row). (c) pass: three wrong codes 400 INVALID_OTP each, the right code after them 403 TOO_MANY_ATTEMPTS, a newly issued code 200. (e) FAIL: signed in through the form at the right clock (Pacific/Honolulu), then the browser clock moved and the page reloaded: +13 h -> sign-in screen, +31 d -> sign-in screen, while Better Auth still knows the session (get-session with the token held before the move) and the session token is gone from the app's store. The client had stored the session cookie with expiry = sign-in + 12 h by the device clock (and the Convex JWT + 15 min). -2 d -> list (pass). A session aged on the server (expiresAt = now - 1 s) with the clock set back 2 d -> sign-in screen (pass). Same +13 h / +31 d result in 3 separate runs (final2, rerun-under-load.log and one earlier re-run) and in the reviewer's probe. Extra variant (not the matrix cell): signing in on a browser whose clock is already +13 h / +31 d / -2 d works and survives a reload; it cannot show a clock-caused sign-out, because the client dates the cookie expiries with that same clock. (d) FAIL, known: TFA-94659 note; requirement wording pending Q17 (isolated backend, no e-mail provider): send-verification-otp answered 200 {success:true}; the backend log shows Better Auth swallowed 'Email delivery is not configured' as a failed background task; the screen says 'Check your email for a 6-digit code. It expires in 5 minutes.' with the code field open and no error.

Product issue: (e) NEW: a physician who signed in normally is signed out when the device clock jumps forward by about 12 h or more (a manual clock change, a wrong time zone corrected, a phone that was off and resyncs): on the next reload the app shows 'Send sign-in code' although the server session is still valid. The web client keeps the session cookie in localStorage with an expiry computed from Max-Age (12 h idle) and the device clock, and drops it once the device clock passes that date. Breaks UAT 3.8 ('A phone with a wrong clock, no clock set, or a different time zone shows the same state as any other device') and the S07 oracle for U3/U4 ('a sign-out caused only by the browser clock = Fail'). (d) known: TFA-94659 note (matrix risk 'Better Auth swallows send errors'); requirement wording pending Q17: when the code e-mail cannot be sent, the screen still says 'Check your email for a 6-digit code. It expires in 5 minutes.' and the physician waits for a code that never comes.

Known gap (known): (d): known: TFA-94659 note; requirement wording pending Q17

Evidence: 17 attached; 1 not attached:

  • newspec-a/rerun-under-load.log — .log files are not attached

Dev run: skipped: local-only — local-only — Lane A runs Tim's Playwright specs, which sign in their own fixture accounts and need the admin key; dev has neither (runner-contract §10), so this runs on the local stack only (Quinn 2026-10-14).. This local result replaces that dev entry (the scenario appears once).
